blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the top of an organisation, cybersecurity stops being a department and becomes a leadership discipline. Attacks do not respect org charts. When a serious incident hits the company, the decisions made in the first hour come from the executive team — not from the security engineers, who are busy doing the technical work. Those decisions include whom to tell, when to tell them, what to say publicly, and how to hold the business together while the response unfolds.

It is essential that senior leaders rehearse these decisions in calm times. A tabletop exercise — a simulated incident run with real people in a real room — is worth ten training videos. It is critical that the people who will make the decisions know each other, know the plan, and know the limits of what they can honestly promise in the first minutes.

Security at the top is not about knowing every threat. It is about being ready — calmly and together — when one of them finally arrives.

items.q: According to the text, who makes the decisions in the first hour of a serious incident?
items.why: "the decisions made in the first hour come from the executive team — not from the security engineers".

items.q: What does the author say a tabletop exercise is worth?
items.why: "A tabletop exercise… is worth ten training videos."

items.q: The phrase "Attacks do not respect org charts" most nearly suggests that…
options: attackers deliberately target the most senior executives
reporting lines should be redrawn after every breach
the security team reports to the wrong department
an incident can cut across departments and force leaders to act outside their usual remit
items.why: Inferência: se o ataque ignora o organograma, a crise não fica contida numa caixa — a liderança precisa agir fora da rotina.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Cybersecurity is best left entirely to the technical specialists.
The first-hour choices are fundamentally leadership choices.
Executive readiness matters more than knowing every possible threat.
Senior leaders should practise their response before a crisis occurs.
items.why: Inferência: a tese do texto é justamente que segurança, no topo, é disciplina de liderança — não um silo técnico.

items.q: Why does the author stress knowing "the limits of what they can honestly promise in the first minutes"?
options: Because the security engineers set the communication rules
Because promises made under pressure without knowing the limits can damage credibility later
Because executives are legally barred from speaking during an incident
Because the first minutes are unimportant to the outcome
items.why: Inferência: conhecer os limites evita prometer o que não se pode cumprir — o que corroeria a confiança conforme a resposta se desenrola.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte conduzindo o exercício simulado. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let's pause the clock there. We are eleven minutes into a simulated ransomware attack, and I want you to notice what just happened in this room, because it is exactly why we run these exercises in calm times.

The moment the scenario said the trading systems were down, three of you reached for your phones to draft a public statement. Nobody had confirmed what was actually encrypted. We must resist that instinct. In a real incident, the first hour belongs to us as a leadership team, not to a press release — and whatever we say publicly, we have to be able to stand behind an hour later.

I also noticed that when I asked who has the authority to pull the payment systems offline, the room went quiet. That silence is the finding. It ought to be one name, agreed in advance, and right now it isn't. So before the next round, I want three things written down: whom we notify, in what order, and the single decision each of you owns.

We are not here to look competent. We are here to discover, calmly and together, exactly which decisions we are not yet ready to make under pressure.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did three members of the team do the moment the trading systems were reported down?
options: They reached for their phones to draft a public statement
items.why: "three of you reached for your phones to draft a public statement."

items.q: According to Charlotte, why does she say "that silence is the finding"?
options: Because no single, pre-agreed person held the authority to pull the payment systems offline
Because the engineers had already solved the problem
Because the team was too tired to answer
items.why: O silêncio revela que ninguém sabia quem tinha autoridade — a lacuna é justamente o que o exercício deveria expor.

items.q: What are the three things Charlotte wants written down before the next round?
options: The passwords, the backups, and the recovery time
Whom to notify, in what order, and the single decision each person owns
The budget, the timeline, and the vendor list
The attacker's demands, the deadline, and the payment method
items.why: "whom we notify, in what order, and the single decision each of you owns."

items.q: What does Charlotte imply by "We are not here to look competent"?
options: The exercise is meant to surface weaknesses, not to reassure people they are already prepared
Competence does not matter in a crisis
The team should hide the exercise from the board
The exercise is purely a formality
items.why: Inferência: o valor do exercício está em descobrir o que ainda falha — não em produzir uma boa impressão.

items.q: Which best describes Charlotte's approach as a facilitator?
options: Composed and diagnostic, using the exercise to expose gaps
Alarmed and improvising as the scenario unfolds
Focused mainly on the technical recovery steps
items.why: Inferência: ela mantém a calma, interrompe o relógio e trata cada falha como um achado a corrigir — postura diagnóstica.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "For the board, security had become a genuine leadership discipline, not a line item in the IT budget." A leadership discipline is…
options: a compulsory training course for engineers
a capability that senior leaders must own and practise, not delegate away
items.why: Leadership discipline = disciplina de liderança: algo que o topo deve dominar e praticar, não delegar.

items.q: "The ransomware crisis began to unfold faster than anyone had modelled." To unfold here means to…
options: develop or play out over time
items.why: To unfold = desenrolar-se: a situação vai se desenvolvendo ao longo do tempo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The whole point of drilling in ___ is that judgement built under calm conditions survives the real pressure."
items.why: Calm times = tempos calmos: ensaiar antes da crise para que a decisão resista sob pressão.

items.q: "A tabletop exercise revealed that no one owned the decision to notify regulators." A tabletop exercise is…
options: a written policy circulated to staff
an audit performed by external consultants
a simulated incident walked through by real decision-makers in a room
a live penetration test of the network
items.why: Tabletop exercise = exercício simulado: as pessoas reais percorrem um incidente fictício numa sala.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Leaders must know the ___ of what they can promise, so they never commit to more than the facts allow."
items.why: Limits = limites: saber até onde se pode prometer para não extrapolar os fatos.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de gestão de crise e segurança. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CEO still has to sign off on the incident-response playbook before we can drill it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the tabletop programme to every business unit this quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, unidade por unidade.

items.q: "When Charlotte named a single decision-owner, two directors pushed back on it." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar por completo.

items.q: "The team agreed the escalation plan in the exercise but never followed through in practice." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Buying yet another monitoring tool won't move the needle if no one owns the first-hour decisions." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
